versions.text: Standard: Components of the air system that do not support a SCF are qualified to the natural and induced environment such that neither normal operations nor physical failure, including installation, of the component adversely impacts safety-critical functionality or the safety of the crewmembers and passengers. This criterion excludes the engine. The minimum environments assessed in this criterion are listed in TABLE III; additional environments may be appropriate for the air system and program being assessed. TABLE III. Natural and induced environments for non-safety-critical components. Environment Natural, Induced, or Both Notes Temperature Natural and Induced Includes the ambient temperatures for all intended ground and flight envelope altitudes, thermal loading from subsystems and components of the air system, and cooling considerations. Pressure Natural and Induced Pressures for all intended ground and flight envelope altitudes. Includes considerations for air vehicle cabin pressurization. Rapid decompression Induced Rapid decompression testing conducted for components in occupied compartments. Acceleration Induced Component retained as installed to prevent injury or damage caused by loose items with exposure to aerodynamic loads, including crash landing loads. Vibration Induced Component retained as installed to prevent injury or damage caused by loose items with exposure to vibration. Includes mechanical, acoustic, and gunfire vibration and addresses the effect of dynamic pressures. Shock Induced Component retained as installed to prevent injury or damage caused by loose items with exposure to the shocks encountered, including catapult launch, arrested landing, and crash landings. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Analysis. (1) Conduct analysis of non-safety-critical components to confirm that neither normal operations nor physical failure, including installation, of the component adversely impacts safety-critical functionality or the safety of crewmembers and passengers. (2) Conduct analysis of post-test data for component qualification testing to identify and assess any failures and design changes (proposed or implemented) to ensure final, tested configuration is understood. (3) Conduct analysis for components qualified by TSO authorization to address differences with air system intended usage, any changes from the original certification, and deviations documented in the TSO authorization to ensure an equivalent level of safety. Analysis identifies environment verification, including those altered or impacted by installation or integration (e.g., vibration and temperature), to be addressed through other MoCs of this criterion. Note: a TSO authorization is not an approval to install and use the component in the air system. (4) Analysis for components that are qualified by similarity address differences in installation, integration, and intended usage from the originally qualified component to ensure an equivalent level of safety. (5) Analysis of available environment verification data for the components confirms neither normal operations nor physical, including installation, failure of the component introduces or propagates a hazard in all intended natural and induced environments. While the analysis addresses any available environment verification data, the minimum data set addresses twice the intended duration of flight test and the environment to be encountered during flight test. The analysis addresses any gaps between actual test data and environmental requirements and any configuration changes made after completion of verification activities, providing an equivalent level of safety assessment. Verification data includes test data, specification sheets, and ICDs that show operation in the intended natural and induced environments. Test. (1) Lab test: Conduct component testing IAW the tailored MIL-STD-810 for a subset of the life cycle of the component and for the minimum environments listed in TABLE III. At a minimum, the testing encompasses the intended duration and environment to be encountered during flight test. Tailoring instructions are contained within MIL-STD-810 with general guidelines in Part One and specific guidelines in each method of Part Two. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Analysis. (6) Analysis of environment verification data for the components confirms neither normal operations nor physical failure, including installation, of the component introduces or propagates a hazard in all intended natural and induced environments. The analysis addresses any gaps between actual test data and environmental requirements and any configuration changes made after completion of verification activities, providing an equivalent level of safety assessment. Verification data includes test data, specification sheets, and ICDs that show operation in the intended natural and induced environments. Test. (2) Lab test: Conduct component testing IAW the tailored MIL-STD-810 for the life cycle of the component, including shipping, transportation, storage, logistics supply, mission use, and sortie use and for the minimum environments listed in TABLE III. Tailoring instructions are contained within MIL-STD-810 with general guidelines in Part One and specific guidelines in each method of Part Two.
